retrievalProfile.description: A centered, multi-colored typographic composition featuring thick, expressive impasto oil paint brushstrokes against a clean, off-white void.
excludeWhen: clean digital vector fonts are required
photorealistic imagery is the primary focus

recipe.visualDefinition: A central typographic cluster where each letter is constructed from thick, visible oil paint strokes (impasto). The letters are irregular, colorful, and tactile, appearing as if sculpted from wet paint. Below the main title, a smaller secondary line of text is rendered in a thin, black, handwritten ink style. The entire composition is isolated on a flat, warm-white background.
coreVisualRelationships: Tactile impasto texture vs. flat minimalist background
Large, colorful painterly letters vs. small, black ink script
Irregular glyph shapes vs. centered formal composition
Vibrant primary/secondary colors vs. neutral off-white negative space
coreInvariants: Visible brush hair textures in the paint

compositionAndHierarchy.subjectPositionAndScale: The main title is centered horizontally and vertically, occupying the middle 60% of the frame. The subtitle is centered directly below it.
compositionAndHierarchy.visualAnchor: The large, multi-colored impasto letters serve as the primary visual anchor.
compositionAndHierarchy.movementAndEyePath: The eye starts at the top-left of the main title, follows the irregular baseline of the painterly letters, and drops to the thin black script below.
compositionAndHierarchy.negativeSpace: Extensive negative space surrounds the central cluster, creating a 'gallery' feel.

colorSystem.contrastColorRole: Multi-colored (letters: red, blue, yellow, green, brown, orange)
colorSystem.saturationAndValueRelationship: High saturation in the paint strokes with varying values to show depth and texture; low saturation background.

typographyAndGraphicLanguage.baseSkeleton: Irregular, chunky sans-serif with varying weights
letterConstructionRules: Letters must be formed by 2-5 distinct, thick brushstrokes
Stroke ends should show 'dry brush' or 'paint drag' effects
Glyphs should overlap slightly or sit very close together
No two letters should share the exact same color pattern
characterSpecificRedesigns: The 'O' or circular forms can include radiating sun-like strokes
Vertical stems should have visible ridges from the brush
typographyAndGraphicLanguage.pairingStrategy: Heavy, textured, multi-colored display type paired with a light, monochromatic, gestural script.
graphicDevices: Dabs of contrasting paint within strokes

candidateDirections.reason: Captures the physical volume of the paint
For the subtitle to maintain the 'artist's signature' look

twoStageComposition.backgroundInstruction: Generate a flat, warm off-white canvas texture with no objects.
twoStageComposition.overlayInstruction: Apply thick, multi-colored impasto oil paint strokes to form the main title letters, ensuring visible brush ridges and physical depth. Below, add a thin, black, gestural handwritten script.

verificationChecks: Is the paint texture visibly raised (impasto)?
Are the colors vibrant and varied within each letter?
Is the background a clean, neutral off-white?
Is the subtitle rendered in a thin, black, handwritten style?

mustRedesign: Exact font skeletons from commercial foundries

mustAchieve: Clean separation between text and background

postGenerationChecks: Confirm the presence of 'dry brush' textures.
Ensure the subtitle is significantly smaller and thinner than the main title.
Check that the colors do not bleed into the background excessively.
